answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering. Each identity accumulates a high-dimensional trace of interaction habits—session cadence, tool-call sequences, error patterns. A fable of uniqueness is not trusted; instead, clustering flags near-identical traces across accounts. To evade, an attacker must make every sybil behave distinctly, an atlas of divergent micro-behaviors that raises orchestration cost far above the value of one account. A single inlet of shared code leaks correlation.
